decisive_items: Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated right ventricular dilatation and an estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg

response.rationale: R1 is the only candidate directly supported by echocardiographic right ventricular strain and pulmonary hypertension with normal coronary arteries, the classic profile of acute pulmonary embolism. R2 shares RV dilatation and normal coronaries but lacks the elevated pulmonary artery pressure and requires an unstated stressor; R3 is contradicted by normal coronary angiography; C1 only adds acute timing to R1 without independent PE-defining raw support.

rejected.why: Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries without stenosis, directly contradicting obstructive acute coronary syndrome; the ST elevation and heparin treatment are nonspecific and also compatible with PE.
Append-only completion of R1; its raw spans only establish acute timing, not pulmonary embolism identity, and it is a correlated restatement of R1.
